functions.description: Parse a mass given as text with a unit (g, kg, mg, lb) into grams as a Decimal.
inputs: mass text with unit

functions.description: Parse a temperature given as text with a unit (K, °C, °F) into kelvin as a Decimal, applying the proper offset.
inputs: temperature text with unit

functions.description: Parse a specific heat given as text with a unit (J/(g·°C), J/(g·K), J/(kg·K), kJ/(kg·K), cal/(g·°C)) into J/(g·K) as a Decimal.
inputs: specific heat text with unit

functions.description: Compute the heat capacity of a body as mass in grams times specific heat in J/(g·K).
inputs: mass in grams
specific heat in J/(g·K)

functions.description: Solve the energy balance for the final temperature as the heat-capacity-weighted average of the initial temperatures.
inputs: heat capacity of the first body in J/K
initial temperature of the first body in K
heat capacity of the second body in J/K
initial temperature of the second body in K

functions.description: Verify that the heat gained by the colder body equals the heat lost by the hotter body at the equilibrium temperature.
inputs: heat capacity of the first body in J/K
initial temperature of the first body in K
heat capacity of the second body in J/K
initial temperature of the second body in K
equilibrium temperature in K

functions.description: Compute the equilibrium temperature of two bodies mixed in an isolated system from their masses, specific heats and initial temperatures.
inputs: the mass of the water (the colder body) with unit
the initial temperature of the water with unit
the mass of the aluminum object (the hot body) with unit
the initial temperature of the aluminum object with unit
the specific heat of aluminum with unit
the specific heat of water with unit

entry_points.text: Find the equilibrium temperature when ●1 of water at ●2 is mixed with a hot ●3 aluminum object at ●4. Specific heats: aluminum ●5, water ●6. Assume the system is isolated.

params.description: the mass of the water (the colder body) with unit
params.validity_range: Positive mass with a mass unit (g, kg, mg, lb); must be greater than zero.

params.description: the initial temperature of the water with unit
params.validity_range: Physical temperature above absolute zero, in K, °C or °F; should be lower than the hot object's temperature for the hot/cold narrative, and the substances should stay in one phase (liquid water roughly 273.15 K to 373.15 K).

params.description: the mass of the aluminum object (the hot body) with unit
params.validity_range: Positive mass with a mass unit (g, kg, mg, lb); must be greater than zero.

params.description: the initial temperature of the aluminum object with unit
params.validity_range: Physical temperature above absolute zero, in K, °C or °F; normally higher than the water's initial temperature; no phase change assumed.

params.description: the specific heat of aluminum with unit
params.validity_range: Positive specific heat with a recognised unit (J/(g·°C), J/(g·K), J/(kg·K), kJ/(kg·K), cal/(g·°C)); aluminum is about 0.9 J/(g·K).

params.description: the specific heat of water with unit
params.validity_range: Positive specific heat with a recognised unit (J/(g·°C), J/(g·K), J/(kg·K), kJ/(kg·K), cal/(g·°C)); liquid water is about 4.18 J/(g·K).
